description: What belongs on a screen and how it is organised. The job a person is doing chooses an archetype; the archetype orders information by priority and disclosure; each kind of data chooses its visualization. Validation reads it to tell a valid screen from a good one: a misleading or unsafe choice is an error, everything else is advice.

report.label: Report
report.for: A finding someone reads and acts on: the conclusion, the evidence, then the detail.

dashboard.label: Dashboard
dashboard.for: A recurring view of how something is doing: headline measures, one principal analysis, supporting comparisons, then positions or records.

transaction.label: Transaction workflow
transaction.for: A consequential change a person reviews and authorizes: what will happen, the evidence, then one decision.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.for: Records a person scans, filters, and works through.

monitoring.label: Monitoring
monitoring.for: The current state of a live system and what changed recently.

comparison.label: Comparison
comparison.for: Options side by side, to choose one.

kpi.label: Headline measures
kpi.rule: Two to four measures in one block, each with its unit and what it is measured against.

time-series.label: One measure over time

avoid.chart-bars: Columns compare a few periods; past a handful they hide the shape of the trend.

misleading.breakdown: A single bar of parts cannot show change over time.
misleading.table: A table of periods hides the trend it is meant to show.
misleading.chart-donut: A ring of parts cannot show change over time.
misleading.treemap: Tiles of parts cannot show change over time.

time-series.rule: Oldest first, on a labelled time axis.

time-series-comparison.label: Actual against a benchmark over time

avoid.chart-bars: Paired columns over many periods are hard to compare; two lines on one scale are not.

misleading.area-chart: An area chart plots one measure; a benchmark needs a second series on the same scale.
misleading.breakdown: A single bar of parts cannot show change over time.

time-series-comparison.rule: Both series on one scale, in one plot, with the benchmark named.

composition.label: Parts of one whole

misleading.line-chart: A line implies an order between parts that have none.
misleading.area-chart: A line implies an order between parts that have none.

composition.rule: Shares of the same total, adding up to 100.

ordered-distribution.label: Ordered buckets, such as maturity or liquidity ladders

avoid.breakdown: One stacked bar loses the order of the buckets and the gaps between them.

misleading.line-chart: A line between buckets implies values between them.
misleading.area-chart: A line between buckets implies values between them.

ordered-distribution.rule: Buckets in their natural order, with inclusive bounds stated in the labels.

category-comparison.label: Two measures per category, such as weight against risk contribution

misleading.breakdown: A breakdown shows one measure; the second one disappears.

category-comparison.rule: Both measures share a scale and a unit.

ranking.label: Categories ranked by one measure
ranking.rule: Largest first, unless the categories have their own order.

records.label: Individual records
records.rule: Readable columns, sortable when there are more than a few rows.

text.label: Explanation
text.rule: Says what the numbers mean; never restates them.

decision.label: A decision or an action
decision.rule: One primary decision, last, naming exactly what will happen.

correlation.label: How two measures relate, such as risk against return

hierarchy.label: Nested parts of a whole
hierarchy.rule: Parts of one whole by size, in at most three groups; values above 0.

matrix.label: A value for every pair of two categories
matrix.rule: One measure in every cell, one value per column in every row.

resolve.label: Resolve pending work
resolve.means: Work through items that wait on this person, in the order that matters, and clear them.

decide.label: Decide
decide.means: Choose between options or approve a change, with the evidence that decides it.

review.label: Review
review.means: Check work someone or something else produced, and accept, correct, or return it.

investigate.label: Investigate
investigate.means: Find out why something happened by following evidence across records.

monitor.label: Monitor
monitor.means: Watch how something is doing over time and notice when it changes.

create.label: Create
create.means: Make something new: a record, a plan, a message.

configure.label: Configure
configure.means: Set how something behaves, rarely, and with confidence about the effect.

priorities.primary: Needed for the immediate task or decision. Visible by default, first in reading order, with the strongest emphasis on the screen.
priorities.supporting: Helps a person understand or complete the task. Visible near the item it supports, or revealed on selection; quieter than primary.
priorities.reference: Useful occasionally, never needed first. Collapsed, in a detail view, or one navigation step away.

disclosures.collapsed: In a closed region a person opens: the label says what is inside and how much.
disclosures.on-selection: Shown for the item a person selected, beside or below it, instead of for every item at once.
disclosures.on-exception: Shown only when something is wrong; when it is, it is visible and never collapsed.
disclosures.elsewhere: Reachable through navigation, an inspector, a drawer, or a detail view; not drawn on this screen.

rules: Information a decision depends on is never collapsed or elsewhere.
An exception that is present is visible; a disclosure that waits on an exception is closed when there is none.
Reference information never sits before primary information in reading order.
Disclosure follows task importance and interaction context, not a maximum word count.

pending-item.label: Pending work
pending-item.means: An approval, ticket, exception, or task waiting on someone.

avoid.card: One card per task turns a queue into a wall of equal boxes and repeats every label.
avoid.stat-row: A count of pending work is not the work; show the items.

entity-profile.label: What the screen is about
entity-profile.means: The client, account, shipment, or project, with the few attributes that orient a person.

avoid.stat-row: Attributes are facts to read, not measures to compare.
avoid.card: The subject of the page is the page; a card around it adds a boundary with nothing outside it.

status.label: Status
status.means: The state of an item, as a word.

avoid.banner: A banner is for an exception; a normal status written as a banner competes with the task.

exception.label: Exception
exception.means: Something wrong that needs attention now.

aggregate-metric.label: Aggregate measure
aggregate-metric.means: A total, rate, or count across many records.

trend.label: Change over time
trend.means: One measure, or a measure and its benchmark, over time.

records.label: Records
records.means: Rows a person scans, compares, or sorts.

source-document.label: Source document
source-document.means: The statement, invoice, contract, or message a value was read from.

extracted-value.label: Extracted value
extracted-value.means: A value read from a source, next to what the record holds.

discrepancy.label: Discrepancy
discrepancy.means: A value that differs between the source and the record.

avoid.text-block: A paragraph about a difference hides the two values; show them side by side.

impact.label: Consequence
impact.means: What a decision changes downstream: a figure, a plan, a person notified.

avoid.text-block: A general summary of what changed is not a consequence; name the value before and after.

alternative.label: Alternatives
alternative.means: Options compared on the same measures to choose one.

setting.label: Setting
setting.means: A preference that changes how something behaves.

avoid.card: A bordered card per option makes every setting look equally important.

explanation.label: Explanation
explanation.means: Why something is so, or what a person should know before acting.

decision.label: Decision
decision.means: The action that resolves the task.

surfaces.description: A boundary around content says it is a separate thing. Each surface has a reason; adding one without the reason adds chrome, not structure.

card.means: A self-contained object that can be read, moved, opened, or acted on alone.
card.reason: The content stands on its own, among peers a person chooses between.

section.means: A titled part of the page. Space and a heading separate it; it has no border.
section.reason: Content belongs to one topic of the page.

record.means: One row of a list or table. Alignment separates records; at most a hairline.
record.reason: Content is one of many items of the same kind.

inset.means: A quieter background inside a section that groups secondary content.
inset.reason: Content is subordinate to what surrounds it, but belongs together.

panel.means: A contextual area beside the main content: the source, the selected item, an inspector.
panel.reason: Content is a different context the person consults while working on the main one.

disclosure.means: A labelled region a person opens and closes.
disclosure.reason: Content is useful occasionally and the label says what it holds.

rules: A boundary needs a reason: an independent object, a different context, a form, or a disclosure.
A card inside a panel or another card repeats a boundary; nest a record or plain content instead, unless the inner card is an object a person acts on alone.
Grouping facts that belong together is the job of a section, an inset, or a list; not of one card per fact.

dividers.description: A divider marks a boundary between things of different kinds. Space, alignment, type, and background separate things of the same kind.
rules: Separation is a property of the layout: sections separate with space and a heading, records with alignment, panels with their own background.
Several closed regions in a row each draw a boundary; group what they hold into one region, or let a section hold what people always need.
A divider never stands in for space between items of the same kind.

task-triage.label: Task triage
task-triage.goal: Resolve pending work in the order that matters.
useWhen: People open the screen to clear what waits on them: approvals, tickets, exceptions, follow-ups.
Items differ in urgency, owner, and next action.
contraindications: Nothing waits on the person; they only watch measures move (use monitoring-dashboard).
There is one item, not a queue (use record-workspace or evidence-review).

zones.label: Needs attention
zones.holds: Only what is overdue or blocked, stated once.

zones.label: Queue
zones.holds: Pending items, most urgent first, each with what is needed, who owns it, and when it is due.

zones.label: Selected item
zones.holds: The context of the item a person is working on.

zones.label: Totals
zones.holds: Counts and trends, for when a person steps back.

layouts.when: Items need context before acting on them, on a wide screen.
Each item can be acted on from its row.

task-triage.responsive: On a narrow screen the queue comes first and the selected item follows it; totals stay collapsed.
states: all clear: say there is nothing waiting and when it was last checked

avoid.reason: Counts of work compete with the work; nobody resolves a number.
A card per task repeats labels and hides the order of urgency.
A banner that restates the queue length is chrome, not an exception.

record-workspace.label: Record workspace
record-workspace.goal: Work on one client, account, project, or shipment: where it stands and what it needs next.
useWhen: The screen is about one entity and the person returns to it to move it forward.
Outstanding decisions on the entity matter more than its full history.
contraindications: The person compares many entities at once (use task-triage or a records table).
The work is checking a document against the record (use evidence-review).

zones.label: Who and where it stands
zones.holds: Name, current stage, owner, and the two or three attributes that orient a person.

zones.label: What needs doing
zones.holds: Open decisions and next steps on this record.

zones.label: Working context
zones.holds: What a person needs while working on the outstanding items.

zones.label: History and details
zones.holds: Activity, documents, and attributes looked up occasionally.

layouts.when: Outstanding work is the main column and the profile sits beside it.
There is little outstanding work; sections in priority order.

record-workspace.responsive: On a narrow screen identity comes first, then what needs doing; context and history follow.
states: nothing outstanding: say so under the identity, and lead with context
blocked: the blocking item leads what needs doing

avoid.reason: A record is read, not monitored; attributes are not headline measures.
Showing every attribute and the whole history at once buries what needs doing.

evidence-review.label: Evidence review
evidence-review.goal: Check values against their source, settle each difference, and confirm what will be saved.
useWhen: Values were read from documents, by people or software, and someone must confirm them.
A wrong value has consequences downstream, so the person needs to see them before saving.
contraindications: There is no source to check against (use record-workspace).
The decision is between alternatives, not about the truth of a value (use comparison-workspace).

zones.label: Source
zones.holds: The document itself, at the place each value comes from.

zones.label: Differences
zones.holds: Each value that differs: what the record holds, what the source says, and what will be saved.

zones.label: What saving changes
zones.holds: The specific values and plans that change downstream.

zones.label: Confirm
zones.holds: One decision that names exactly what will be saved.

zones.label: Matched values
zones.holds: Values that agree, for completeness.

layouts.when: A wide screen: the source stays in view while values are checked.
A narrow screen: each difference names its place in the source.

evidence-review.responsive: On a narrow screen differences come first and the source follows, each difference naming the page and line it comes from.
states: no differences: say every value matches and offer to confirm
unresolved: confirmation names what is still open
saved: show the saved values, not the form

avoid.reason: A paragraph about what changed hides the two values; show them side by side.
Values that agree push the differences out of view.
Confirming without seeing the consequences is not an informed decision.

comparison-workspace.label: Comparison workspace
comparison-workspace.goal: Choose between alternatives on the measures that matter.
useWhen: Two to four options are compared on the same measures, and one will be chosen.
Tradeoffs matter more than any single figure.
contraindications: There is only one option to approve (use evidence-review or an approval).
More than a handful of options: rank them in a table first.

zones.label: How they differ
zones.holds: The measures that differ, on shared scales, with the better value named in words.

zones.label: Choice
zones.holds: Choose one, naming what follows.

zones.label: What they share
zones.holds: Measures that do not differ, for completeness.

layouts.when: One comparison table, then the choice.
Each option is chosen as a card with its key differences.

comparison-workspace.responsive: On a narrow screen options keep a shared scale; the table scrolls horizontally rather than stacking options apart.
states: tie: say which measure decides it
chosen: show the choice and what follows

avoid.reason: Options on separate cards with different measures cannot be compared.
Headline numbers per option repeat what the comparison shows.

configuration-workspace.label: Configuration workspace
configuration-workspace.goal: Set how something behaves, with frequent settings first and advanced ones out of the way.
useWhen: People change preferences that affect behaviour, mostly rarely.
Settings group into a few mental models: who, when, what, how much.
contraindications: A one-off choice inside a task (put the control in the task).

zones.label: Common settings
zones.holds: The settings most people change, grouped by what they control, with good defaults.

zones.label: Advanced
zones.holds: Settings few people change, revealed when relevant.

zones.label: Irreversible
zones.holds: Destructive actions, separate and confirmed.

layouts.when: One form per group, each with its own save.

configuration-workspace.responsive: Groups stack; labels stay above controls on a narrow screen.
states: unsaved changes: name them by the save button

avoid.reason: A bordered card per option makes every setting look equally important and doubles the scroll.
All settings at once hide the few that matter.

monitoring-dashboard.label: Monitoring dashboard
monitoring-dashboard.goal: See how something is doing over time and notice when it changes.
useWhen: People return regularly to see how measures move, and act only when one changes.
contraindications: People open it to resolve work; the measures are a by-product (use task-triage).

zones.label: Headline measures
zones.holds: Two to four measures, each with its comparison.

zones.label: Principal analysis
zones.holds: How the main measure moves or splits.

zones.label: Records
zones.holds: The records behind the numbers.

zones.label: Sources
zones.holds: Where the numbers come from.

layouts.when: The reference order for a dashboard.

monitoring-dashboard.responsive: Measures wrap two by two on a narrow screen; charts keep their labels.
states: partial data: say which sources are missing

avoid.reason: More than one block of headline numbers competes for attention.

analytical-report.label: Analytical report
analytical-report.goal: Read a finding, the evidence behind it, and act on it.
useWhen: A conclusion has to be trusted before someone acts on it.
contraindications: The reader needs to act on many items (use task-triage).

zones.label: Finding
zones.holds: The conclusion in a sentence, with its key figure.

zones.label: Evidence
zones.holds: The analysis that supports the finding.

zones.label: Detail
zones.holds: Provenance and full records.

layouts.when: A report reads from the conclusion down.

states: inconclusive: say what evidence is missing

avoid.reason: A reader should not assemble the conclusion from charts.

lint.description: Rules the composition linter applies. Errors are invalid or unsafe compositions; warnings are probable problems in hierarchy, grouping, redundancy, or disclosure; suggestions are improvements where several good answers exist. Every rule is deterministic: it reads the screen, the plan, and the registry, never a model.

plan-invalid.means: The composition plan does not match plan.schema.json.

plan-unknown-node.means: The plan names a node the screen does not have.

hidden-decision-input.means: Information the plan marks as primary sits in a closed region, so a person decides without it.

hidden-exception.means: An exception that is present is collapsed.

decision-without-impact.means: A consequential decision on an evidence review shows no consequences before it is confirmed.

competing-primary-actions.means: More than one primary decision on one screen part.

kpi-grid-on-task-screen.means: Headline measure blocks on a screen whose job is to resolve, review, or configure, without a decision that depends on them.

archetype-mismatch.means: The archetype the plan declares does not serve the job it declares.

priority-order.means: Reference or supporting information comes before primary information.

competing-emphasis.means: More parts claim primary emphasis than a person can scan first.

nested-surface.means: A card-like component inside a panel, inset, or card repeats a boundary.

card-as-grouping.means: Several cards each hold one fact that a list or table would group.

unranked-queue.means: A queue of pending work gives no order, due date, or priority to act on.

restated-content.means: Explanatory text repeats figures or labels already shown beside it.

repeated-label.means: A heading repeats the title of the only part under it.

banner-without-exception.means: A banner states something that is not an exception.

stacked-disclosures.means: Several closed regions in a row, each with its own boundary.

supporting-expanded.means: Reference information is open by default.

dense-record.means: A compact record carries more attributes than a person scans.

action-per-card.means: Each of several cards carries its own button, so no action leads.

missing-plan.means: No composition plan: the screen cannot be checked against the job it serves.

criteria.label: Task prominence
criteria.means: The work a person came to do is first and strongest.

criteria.label: Information architecture
criteria.means: Information is ordered by priority: primary, then supporting, then reference.

criteria.label: Progressive disclosure
criteria.means: Reference is one step away; what a decision needs is never hidden.

criteria.label: Content economy
criteria.means: Each fact appears once; text explains instead of restating.

criteria.label: Component appropriateness
criteria.means: Components are chosen for the job, not because they are available.

criteria.label: Surface economy
criteria.means: Every boundary has a reason; grouping uses space and lists before boxes.

criteria.label: Structural grouping
criteria.means: Emphasis and grouping make one reading order obvious.

criteria.label: Action clarity
criteria.means: One primary action per part, naming what will happen, with its consequences in view.

criteria.label: Fit to the job
criteria.means: The composition archetype serves the job the plan declares.

criteria.label: Plan contract
criteria.means: The plan is valid and names nodes that exist.

criteria.label: Responsive behaviour
criteria.means: Checked in a rendered review: deterministic rules cannot see layout at each width.

criteria.label: Accessibility
criteria.means: Component contracts check names and roles; contrast and focus order need a rendered review.

cues.description: Words that hint at a job, a subject, or a term in a request. They only raise questions and order a provisional plan: a word is not an intent, so a plan that rests on cues alone has status needs-context.

terms.dashboard: “Dashboard” names a place people open, not a layout. The job decides whether it is a monitoring dashboard, a work queue, or a record.
terms.overview: An overview is a summary of something; the job decides what summary serves it.
terms.home: A home screen serves whatever people most often come to do first.
terms.portal: A portal is a place; the job decides its layout.
